html:
The Act of Supremacy of 1534 was a law of the English Parliament that made King Henry VIII the "Supreme Head" of the church in England. It cut the English church off from the authority of the pope in Rome.

The trigger was Henry's marriage. He wanted to end his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, who had not given him a son, and the pope refused. Henry married Anne Boleyn anyway in 1533, and Parliament passed a string of laws that put the king above the church. Officials had to swear an oath to accept this. Thomas More refused and was executed in 1535.

The act opened the way to the dissolution of the monasteries, which moved huge lands from the church to the crown and its friends. Henry's break was more about power than belief, but it came in the years of the Reformation that Martin Luther had started. Mary I repealed the act; Elizabeth I passed a new one in 1559, which made the monarch "Supreme Governor" of the Church of England.
sum: The Act of Supremacy of 1534 was a law of the English Parliament that made King Henry VIII the "Supreme Head" of the church in England. It cut the English church off from the authority of the pope in Rome.
